title: view_resume_page is a third parallel copy of the form assembly — script tail and section list now drift across three sites
evidence:
form_sections.view_section_about_you(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_your_situation(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_work_income(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_references(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_guarantor(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_tell_us_more(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_documents(values:, errors: []),
              form_sections.view_section_review_consent(errors: []),
              form_view.view_honeypot_field(), ... plus the identical 4-script tail (form.js, form_stepper.js, view_apply_analytics_script(), view_draft_saver_script()) repeated at form_view.gleam:109, form_pages.gleam:371 and form_pages.gleam:462
detail: The same 8-section list, honeypot/timing fields and 4-script tail are now hand-maintained in view_application_page, view_form_with_errors and view_resume_page. This PR itself demonstrates the drift mechanism: adding the draft saver required editing all three sites; missing one silently disables saves on that render.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared form_sections_all(values, errors) list and a form_script_tail() helper in form_view, and call both from the three page assemblies.

title: draft_handler imports application_handler for one pure predicate — first handler→handler import outside the router
detail: is_accepting_applications is a pure predicate over sql.GetVacancyForFormRow, yet the new module now depends on a 2416-line god-module to reach it. Housing the predicate beside the row type (application/sql) keeps handlers decoupled and avoids blessing further cross-handler imports.
recommended_fix: Move is_accepting_applications into application/sql.gleam (or domain_helpers) and have both handlers import it from there.

title: Draft JSON handlers skip the defense-in-depth wisp body-cap pin that process_form_submission establishes
evidence: application_handler.gleam:157-164: "// Defense in depth: pin wisp's own body + files quotas to the middleware intent. The middleware body-size gate already rejects oversize requests upstream, but if anything bypasses that path (e.g. a future wiring change) wisp itself won't parse beyond 22 MB." |> wisp.set_max_body_size(middleware.max_upload_body_size) — grep shows no set_max_body_size anywhere in draft_handler.gleam; wisp's internal.gleam default is max_body_size: 8_000_000
detail: handle_save_draft/handle_continue_link rely solely on the middleware 64 KB gate; if that wiring regresses, wisp's 8 MB default applies on an unauthenticated endpoint. The sibling multipart handler explicitly pins its cap for exactly this scenario, so the pattern exists one module away.
recommended_fix: Add |> wisp.set_max_body_size(middleware.max_draft_body_size) on the request in handle_save_draft and handle_continue_link before wisp.require_json.
